hyps.why: Replacing avg_pool with a 3x3 conv on the direct input-output edge gains less than the average upgrade (1.76/0.98/5.70 vs ~2.8/2.8/8.7).
Replacing the skip on edge 3 with a 3x3 conv gives little gain (0.96/-0.02/3.67), since the residual path is already valuable.
Filling a missing direct edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole new path and gives the largest gains (3.82/6.50/17.47).
With a skip on edge 3, upgrading edge 4 to a 3x3 conv gains less (1.28/2.22/4.23 vs ~2.85/5.08/8.77).
With a skip on edge 3, upgrading edge 5 to a 3x3 conv gains less (1.85/2.92/4.73 vs ~2.9/4.0/8.1).
With the direct edge removed, edge 5 carries more of the output path, so upgrading it gains more (3.08/5.46/14.67).
With edge 0 removed, node 1 gets no input, so the edge 1->2 upgrade does nothing (0.40/0.22/-0.23).
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is disconnected from the input, so upgrading edge 4 gives almost nothing (0.56/-0.44/0.83).
With edge 5 removed, node 2 cannot reach the output, so the edge 1 upgrade has almost no effect (-0.84/0.68/0.53).
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip on edge 5 loses a lot (-2.71/-4.46/-8.77), while replacing a 1x1 conv loses far less.
